title: Finite semigroup-dressed Petz collar discriminator
question: Does a rank-preserving heat-semigroup collar give a finite, dimension-safe normalized-filter and Petz transport interface that is more stable than a hard spectral projector?

model.tripartition: A=core, B=buffer, C=environment, with omitted exterior traced out
model.shifted_energy: K_A=H_A-inf(sigma(H_A)) is positive on every finite local core
model.filtered_state: sigma_s=(F_s tensor I_BC) rho_ABC (F_s tensor I_BC) / m_s
model.candidate_disturbance: D(rho,sigma_s) <= sqrt(1-m_s)+(1-m_s)/2 is tested as a finite candidate envelope, not assumed analytically

lean_crosscheck.boundary: Lean checks scalar exponential, semigroup and triangle arithmetic only; finite matrices, moment uniformity and all QFT transfers remain Python/open analysis.

theorem_ladder.name: finite smooth-filter positivity and mass control
dimension-free normalized-filter disturbance
theorem_ladder.boundary: cutoff-independent moment and analytic theorem open

theorem_ladder.name: Euclidean collar to common dynamics
theorem_ladder.boundary: OS/KMS/GNS and Lorentzian continuation not tested here

adversarial_review.check: Every filtered state is divided by its measured mass and raw-state trace is retained.
adversarial_review.disposition: PASS FINITELY; UNIFORM LOWER MASS OPEN

adversarial_review.check: The exact mass defect is compared with the measured first moment; no cutoff-independent moment is inserted.
F_s is built from shifted local spectral values and semigroup composition is checked before Petz recovery.
One Petz map is built from the filtered BC and B marginals and reused for both filtered and original inputs.
The collar parameter is not identified with physical time or a causal cone.

promotion_criteria: A cutoff-independent local first-moment estimate on a declared common core
A proved dimension-safe normalized-filter modulus with explicit hypotheses
Separate OS/KMS/GNS and common-alpha continuation evidence
stop_conditions: If the mass collapses or the candidate disturbance grows under every admissible scale, retire the smooth route beyond its finite identities.
If the finite candidate envelope fails, retain only the mass and semigroup identities and do not promote normalized-filter transport.
If all stable moduli require a logarithmic dimension factor, keep the route finite and claim-nonbearing.
If no common Euclidean form core or real-time continuation is available, keep this as an OS-side collar only.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite semigroup-dressed Petz collar only. It proves no QCMI upper bound, cutoff-independent moment, common core, common-alpha convergence, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A result.
no_overclaim: A finite smooth filter can remove rank jumps and satisfy scalar mass/semigroup identities without supplying a uniform normalized disturbance, a physical time generator or any Clay-level closure.
